chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadda', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbid the use of narcissus (daffodil). So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Why is that?' He said: 'Because it is the aroma of the non-Arabs.' And one of our companions informed me that the non-Arabs used to smell it when they were fasting, and said, 'It restrains hunger.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.النَّرْجِس: Narcissus (daffodil), a flower used for its scent

ai.seo_question: Why is narcissus perfume prohibited or disliked in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits narcissus by identifying it as 'rihan al-a'ajim' (the perfume of the non-Arabs/Persians), illustrating the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'Istishab al-'Adah' (presumption of custom) where specific sensory practices are discouraged if they mimic pre-Islamic or foreign rituals. This ruling underscores the importance of distinguishing Islamic worship from cultural assimilation, ensuring that acts of devotion remain distinct from the customs of other communities.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Dawood Bin Is’haq Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> forbid from the daffodils. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Why is that so?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because it is an aroma of the non-Arabs’. And, one of our companions informed me that the non-Arabs used to smell it when they were Fasting, and said, ‘It restrains the hunger’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadhdha’ from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, prohibiting the use of Narcissus. I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, why is that? He (the Imam) said, ’Because it is the perfume of non- Arabs.’
Certain persons of our people have narrated that non- Arabs wear this perfume when fasting and say that it suppresses hunger.’”
